texts: The washerman at our ghat scrubs other people's clothes all day, sees the clouds gather and clear, and goes home untouched by any of it; I'd like a doha about living like that.
doha with a washerman and a cloud, about living in the world but staying untouched
Write a doha where a washerman does his daily work amid the dirt of the world while a cloud passes overhead, and he stays clean in spirit, living fully but clinging to nothing.
washerman, cloud, untouched
The washerman handles the world's stains and the cloud drifts over them all, and neither is marked by what it meets.
I have a demanding job, a family and a loan to pay, and I want a doha that teaches how to live fully in all of it without letting any of it take hold of my inner peace.
Walk through the busyness of life with open hands and a quiet heart, and let it pass through you without a trace.
doha about being in the world but not of it
in the world, untouched
My boss screamed at the team all morning, and my friend just carried on with his work, calm as ever, as if none of it could reach him.
bridge, passing through
Every morning I cross the bridge to a job I take seriously, yet I try to remember it is only a place I pass through, not a place I belong.
Please write a doha about the bridge that carries one through the world's busyness, where the wise traveller does his work and meets his people but does not build a home on the bridge itself.
The bridge serves all who cross and keeps none, and the wise heart serves the world and keeps no hold on it.
doha with a bridge, about living in the world while staying detached
The tree gives fruit and shade to all and clings to none, and the tongue speaks and holds no grudge: so lives the free heart in the world.
doha with a tree and a tongue, about being in the world without being caught by it
tree, tongue, untouched
My grandfather speaks warmly with everyone, gives freely under the old tree in our yard, and never seems to hold on to a slight or a gain.
Write a doha where a tree gives everything and holds nothing, and a tongue speaks without bitterness, to show a person who lives among people and things without being held by any of them.
My friend plays with his kids, runs his business and cooks dinner like everyone else, but when his parrot flew away and when a relative died, he stayed oddly calm and gentle; I'd love a doha on that.
parrot, skeleton, untouched
The parrot chatters of the world and the skeleton keeps silent, and the wise one is between, fully alive and fully free.
Write a doha where a parrot repeats the world's talk and a skeleton lies in the corner as a reminder, and the householder goes about his day among both, engaged but never clinging to any of it.
doha with a parrot and a skeleton, about living in the world without clinging
I get promoted, I miss a promotion, and my mother says it's all the same weather to the sky; I want a doha that captures that lightness.
doha about doing your job properly but not being attached to the result
Do the work with all your heart, and release it when it is done, for the wise let the result fall where it will.
Please write a doha about a person who takes part fully in family, work and community life, laughing and weeping with the others, but who inwardly keeps a space that none of it can bind.
working without clinging
When my father lost his savings in a bad deal he sat quietly for an hour, then went back to work with the same smile; I'd love a doha about that kind of calm.
doha about enjoying life without getting stuck on any of it
unbound while living
He walks among joys and sorrows as a guest among hosts, tasting and thanking, and taking nothing home.
Write a doha about the householder who looks after his duties with love but inwardly stays free, so that gain and loss, praise and blame touch him as little as the passing seasons touch the sky.
doha with scales, about doing business without getting attached to profit
At my family's grocery, the scales have gone up and down for forty years, and my uncle weighs out each sale with care and then forgets it, free from every profit and loss.
Write a doha about a trader who weighs everything fairly on his scales, takes part fully in the business of life, and yet leaves each sale behind in his mind, untouched by gain or loss.
scales, balanced mind
The scales weigh gain and loss, and the one who holds them is not weighed down, for his heart stays level.
doha about living in the world but not letting it stick to you

Please write a doha about the quiet wisdom of a person who raises a family, earns his living, and meets every joy and sorrow with full presence, yet remains inwardly untouched, like a guest in his own life.
engaged but unattached
Plunged in the world's bustle, the wise heart remains dry, and the sorrows of the day slide off it.
My mother goes through a hundred little crises a day with a steady smile, and nothing seems to leave a mark on her.
doha on being involved in life but not tangled up in it
free in the crowd
A guest in the great hall of the world, the wise one eats and sings and leaves with only a thank you.
Please write a doha about how someone can love their family, do their work, and enjoy the festival without being caught by it, taking the world as a visitor takes a night's welcome.
At a loud family wedding, with everyone arguing and laughing, my uncle sat calmly, joined in everything, and somehow seemed to float above it all.
The date palm stands beside the ocean's edge, lifting its head to the sky, untouched by the spray.
date palm, ocean, untouched
Write a doha where a date palm stands by the shore of the ocean, bathed in spray yet bearing sweet fruit, and the wise one, living among the waves of the world, bears sweetness without being drowned.
doha with a date palm and the ocean, about being untouched by the world around you
We live by the ocean in a salty, noisy town, and my neighbour, who grows a single date palm in his yard, stays calm and cheerful in the middle of it all.
My colleague went through a divorce, a job change and a move in one year, and kept on being gentle and clear, as if the storms passed through him without a trace.

I would like a doha about a person who lives in the busiest part of life, with its demands and its quarrels, yet inwardly remains unmoved, like something that was never wetted by the rains that fell upon it.
unmoved in the storm
Storms of gain and loss go by, and the heart that does not cling remains as clear as morning.
doha on staying calm and free while life goes on around you
tongue, shroud, untouched
My uncle's tongue was always sweet to everyone, and when he was wrapped in a shroud he looked as if he had left the world a long time before; I want a doha on living and leaving without clinging.
Write a doha where the tongue speaks kindly to all and the shroud awaits all, and the wise man lives between them in the world's affairs, loving and laughing and clinging to neither.
The tongue sings of the world and the shroud waits for the singer, and the wise one lives lightly between them.
doha with a tongue and a shroud, about living in the world without clinging
The grindstone grinds all day, turning grain into flour, and yet it is not changed by what it grinds; write a doha about a person who works in the busy world and is not changed by its gain or loss.
doha with a grindstone, about working in the world without being worn down by it
The grindstone turns the grain, yet takes no grain for itself, and so lives the wise in the world's work.
My mother has run our home for forty years, doing a hundred tasks each day, and she tells me she has never taken any of them to heart.
grindstone, unclinging work
The oil press yields its oil and the bitter gourd its bitterness, and the wise one takes what comes with no hold on either.
doha with an oil press and a bitter gourd, about taking life as it comes and not clinging
oil press, bitter gourd, unattached
My dad works long hours at his oil press and eats whatever is served at night, bitter gourd or sweet, and seems to hold onto neither the day's trouble nor its triumph.
Write a doha where the oil press works all day and the bitter gourd is eaten at night, and the wise householder accepts both the labour and the bitterness without holding on to either as his own.
living lightly
Please write a doha for someone who must live fully in a busy family and workplace, who loves deeply, and who still wishes to keep the heart free so that nothing, not praise nor insult, binds it.
Live in the world, love in the world, and yet let the heart rest in a place the world cannot reach.
At my cousin's big family gathering, she managed everyone's needs for hours and then sat quietly alone, unbothered by the gossip.
write a doha about being in the world but not of it
palace, unattached king
doha with a palace, about someone who rules but isn't attached
A king lives in his palace, governs his kingdom with care, and yet does not call any of it his own in his heart; please write a doha about this inner freedom within outward duty.
The king rules in the palace and the ruler within rules himself: this is the one who is truly free.
My friend became a manager in a huge corporate palace of an office, and while he works with great care, he seems not to take any of it personally.
A swan swims through the muddy lake with white feathers that no stain can hold, and a man holding gold in his hand lets it pass through like water; please write a doha about living untouched.
swan, gold, untouched
My neighbour handles other people's gold all day as a jeweller, glides through the crowd with a calm like a swan's, and never lets a single piece cling to his heart.
doha with a swan and gold, about being in the world but not attached
The swan glides through the mud and rises white, the gold passes through the hand and leaves no mark.
The touchstone tests every metal that is rubbed against it and keeps none of them; write a doha that shows how the wise one meets all the world's offerings and holds nothing in his heart.
doha with a touchstone, about meeting everything in life without holding on
The touchstone meets the precious and the plain alike and keeps neither, and so should the heart meet the world.
My work brings me in touch with hundreds of clients a week, and I try to be like a touchstone, testing and moving on without carrying any of them home.
touchstone, unclinging heart
doha with a lion, about living bravely in the world but not clinging
lion, free in the world
A lion walks through the world with no fear and no hoard, hunting only what it needs and leaving the rest, and I want a doha about that kind of inner freedom within an active life.
The lion takes what it needs and walks on, and the hunger and the hunt both fall behind.
My boss walks into every tough negotiation like a lion, wins or loses, and sleeps soundly, never carrying the result in his chest.

The rainbird drinks only the drops that fall from the sky and the old man with the forehead mark takes only what comes to him, and neither clings; please write a doha on living in the world with such freedom.
rainbird, forehead mark, unclinging
My uncle wears a mark on his forehead and runs a busy business, but like a rainbird that drinks only the rain, he takes only what comes and clings to nothing.
The rainbird waits for the first drop, the mark on the brow rests quiet, and the heart takes what comes and holds nothing.
doha with a rainbird and a forehead mark, about living in the world without attachment
doha with a mosque and a temple, about living in the world with no attachment to either
My neighbour visits both the mosque and the temple, works his full day, and goes home to his family with the same calm, belonging to none of it and loving all of it.
The mosque and the temple both stand in the world's street, and the free heart walks past both, untouched and unsullied.
Please write a doha about the one who prays in the mosque, bows at the temple, works hard in the world, and yet keeps his heart from sticking to any of it, being free in all of it.
mosque, temple, free heart
The wise one moves through the crowd of wanting and is not carried off, for he is free of its pull.
doha on enjoying the world but not needing it
unbound, yet present
My sister enjoys parties and promotions, but when they end she is as cheerful as before, and I envy her lightness.

Please write a doha for a person who takes part in all the pleasures and pains of the world with open eyes, yet inwardly leaves each one behind as soon as it ends, as a passing traveller leaves the road.
The cuckoo sings in the moneylender's garden and flies away, taking neither his coins nor his cares.
Write a doha where a moneylender counts his interest in the shade while a cuckoo sings above him, and the singer, free of all counting, shows what it is to live in the world and cling to nothing.
cuckoo, moneylender, untouched
The moneylender in the next lane spends all day worrying over interest, while a cuckoo sings on his roof, free as ever; I'd like a doha about being the cuckoo.
doha with a cuckoo and a moneylender, about being free while living among money
An oil press turns all day at the centre of the village, yet no drop of oil sticks to the heart of the man who works it. Please write a doha about doing the world's labour without being bound.
doha with an oil press, about doing your work but not being attached
The oil press turns and oil pours out, yet the master of the press remains dry and unmoved.
My brother runs the family oil press with great devotion but has told me that he never loses sleep over a bad month.
oil press, unclinging worker
not clinging, not leaving
I'd like a doha about the middle path of a person who neither runs away from family and work nor gets stuck in them, but lives with one foot in the world and the heart free.
doha on living in the world without clinging to it
I've been told to either renounce the world or enjoy it fully, but I wish to live in it without becoming entangled; please give me a doha.
Neither flee the world nor be seized by it; walk through it with an open and a quiet heart.
The winnowing fan in my grandmother's hand sorts the grain from the chaff, and under the morning sun she does all things with a calm that sorts the useful from the useless in her own mind.
The winnowing fan separates the grain, the sun shines on all, and the wise one lives in the world, keeping what serves and releasing what clings.
doha with a winnowing fan and the sun, about being in the world but not clinging
winnowing fan, sun, discernment
Write a doha where a winnowing fan lifts the chaff from the grain in the open sunlight, and the wise person, living among all things, lets the useless fall away and holds on to nothing at all.
When the company laid off half the staff, one colleague kept doing his work with the same attention, saying only, it was never mine; I want a doha to describe that mind.
doha about doing everything fully but expecting nothing
Please write a doha about the person who does his full duty to the world, plays his part in every scene of family and work, and yet when it all ends, walks away without a sense of loss.
Play the part with all your heart, and when the play is done, leave it gladly.
free in the midst
The wise one goes among people as a breeze goes among them, touching all and held by none.
touched by nothing

I want a doha about the quiet strength of someone who is present in every conversation, every responsibility, and every gathering, but who is never possessed by them, so that the heart stays at home within itself.
My aunt manages the whole family's affairs without ever seeming to be pulled into the dramas around her.
doha for someone who wants to be in the world yet not be stuck in it
The cuckoo's song and the arrow's flight both pass through the air, and neither stays; so passes the free heart through the world.
cuckoo, arrow, passing through
The arrow of the day's work flies, the cuckoo sings at dusk, and my teacher says that he has lived all his life like the flight, doing what must be done and not looking back.
Write a doha where an archer lets his arrow go and then listens to the cuckoo without any thought of where it landed, showing how the wise one acts in the world and then releases the result.
doha with a cuckoo and an arrow, about doing your part and letting go
Our yogi neighbour works as a clerk during the day, rings a bell at dusk, and says that neither the office nor the bell has ever held him; I'd love a doha on this.
The bell rings out over the town, the yogi hears it and smiles, for he lives in the world as if already beyond it.
doha with a yogi and a bell, about living in the world with the heart free
yogi, bell, unclinging
Write a doha where a yogi lives in the middle of a busy town, rings his bell at dusk, goes about the world's business, and remains untouched by any of it, like the sound that fades after the bell.
She runs a household of ten, works full time and still keeps a quiet space inside that no demand ever reaches; I'd like a doha on this woman.
engaged, yet free
doha on loving life without being attached to it
Please write a doha about the grace of a person who throws himself into worldly work and worldly love and still, at the centre, rests in a calm that nothing coming or going can disturb.
In the thick of the world's bustle, he keeps a still place within, and the world's tumult passes outside it.
The prayer beads slip through the fingers and the days slip through the world, and the wise one lets both pass.
prayer beads, passing days

Write a doha where a householder tells his prayer beads in the evening after a long day among people and money, and as each bead passes through his fingers he lets the day's gains and losses pass too.
doha with prayer beads, about living in the world without holding on
After a hard day at work my mother sits with her prayer beads and lets the day go bead by bead, and she is always so calm after.
A parrot sits amid a household full of noise and repeats the words it hears, but the wise man, though he lives in the same noise, speaks only what is needed and does not take in the rest.
The parrot repeats what it hears and is caught in the words, while the wise one lets the world's chatter pass over him.
doha with a parrot, about hearing everything in the world and not letting it stick
In the office of gossip and tension, my friend listens like a parrot to all of it but never repeats it, never takes it inside.
parrot, unaffected
A woman sits at her spinning wheel making cloth fibre for the family while the arrow of time flies overhead, and she works with a calm that clings neither to the work nor to the passing days.
doha with a spinning wheel and an arrow, about doing the daily work without clinging
The wheel turns and the arrow flies, and the wise spinner does her work while her heart rests far from both.
My grandmother spins at her wheel every morning and says each day passes like an arrow, and she lives it with a smile and no grasping.
spinning wheel, arrow, unclinging
doha with a mosque and potter and clay, about living in the world with the heart free
A potter in our town shapes clay all day, prays at the mosque on Fridays, and is the most unattached person I know; I'd love a doha about him.
mosque, potter and clay, free
Write a doha where a potter shapes clay with his hands and then walks to the mosque, giving his whole self to the work and the prayer and yet holding on to neither, free in both.
The potter shapes the clay and bows at the mosque, and in both he is fully present and in neither is he bound.
Walking home beneath the moon after a long day of negotiations, I felt that the whole day, with all its wins and losses, was as light as moonlight on the road.
doha with the moon, about doing your work and then letting it all go
Write a doha about a person who has spent the day in the heat of the world's affairs and walks home beneath the moon, setting down everything he did as if it had happened to someone else.
moon, letting go
The moon moves over the world's affairs and takes nothing from any of them, and the wise heart does the same.
A peacock dances in the branches of a tree, delighted by the rain and the world, yet clings to no branch for long; please write a doha about someone who enjoys life fully but lives lightly.
doha with a tree and a peacock, about enjoying life but not clinging
tree, peacock, light-hearted
The peacock dances and leaves the tree, the tree gives and keeps nothing, and the heart that does the same is free.
My friend is the life of every party, dances until midnight, and then is gone, without regrets or hangover of the heart, like a peacock that leaves the tree.
At my grandfather's funeral, someone said he had lived in the world like a man already wrapped in a shroud, loving it but never holding it; I'd like a doha on that.
The shroud waits, and the wise one lives in the world as if he had already put it on, light and free of every claim.
doha with a shroud, about living in the world without clinging to it
Write a doha about a person who handles the world's affairs with care and tenderness, but whose heart is already light enough to put on a shroud and leave with no sense of loss.
shroud, unclinging life
A date palm stands in the courtyard bearing sweet fruit for all, while a crow flies off with a date, and neither the palm nor the bird clings to the other; please write a doha on this lightness.
doha with a date palm and a crow, about living freely in the world
date palm, crow, unclinging
The date palm gives its fruit and does not hold it, the crow takes it and does not keep it, and so the world moves lightly.
Our date palm gives fruit to the whole street, including the crows, and my father, who tends it, never counts what is taken.
Ash on the brow is the sign of one who has let the world burn through him and keeps nothing of it.
doha with ash, about living in the world untouched by it
Write a doha about the wise one who walks in the world's bustle with a smear of ash on his forehead, a reminder that all burns and nothing is held, and he lives his daily life fully but untouched.
ash, untouched
My uncle works in the hardware store, laughs with his customers, and puts a line of ash on his forehead each morning to remember it is all passing.
The house is built of stone, and the wise one lives in it as a guest for the night, using it with gratitude and leaving without a tear.
When we had to sell the old house, my father picked up a stone from the garden, smiled, and said it was a good place to stay, and then he walked away; I'd like a doha on that.
house, stone, unclinging
Write a doha where a householder lives in a house of stone, tending it with love and care, yet knows in his heart that it is a lodging for the night, and feels no loss when he leaves.
doha with a house and a stone, about living in a home without being attached
When my business thrived and when it failed, my mother's voice on the phone was the same warm voice, as though neither ever touched her.
Praise comes and goes, blame comes and goes, and the wise heart stays as it was.
doha on staying the same whether you win or lose
Please write a doha about the person who lives with equal calm in good fortune and bad, in praise and blame, doing his best in the world and holding on to none of its results.
even-minded, unclinging
Do your work as one who serves, then let go, for what was given was never yours to hold.
After the project I had worked on for two years was cancelled, I surprised myself by feeling light, and my team asked how I could be so calm.
Please write a doha for someone who gives everything to their work and family, with full love and full effort, but then lets go of the outcome and rests in a peace that the result cannot touch.
work, then release
doha about letting go of the results of your work
By the ocean, a tortoise on the rocks draws into its shell whenever a big wave comes, and I thought of my dad, who stays calm in the middle of the family's biggest storms.
doha with an ocean and a tortoise, about staying calm in the middle of the world's storms

Write a doha where a tortoise sits by the great ocean, drawing its limbs inward when the waves strike, and the wise one does the same in the world's storms, drawing the heart inward and staying free of the tumult.
ocean, tortoise, inward calm
The ocean thunders and the tortoise draws in, and the heart that has learned this walks through every storm untouched.

I'd like a doha about a person who lives in the busy centre of family, work and society, joining its celebrations and mourning its losses, yet never so entangled that he forgets the freedom at his core.
The wise one is in the crowd yet apart from it, quiet within the noise.
in, not of
doha about being involved without being attached
People think I'm cold because I stay calm at crises, but I just try to take part without sinking into things.
doha with a moth, about being drawn to the world but not burning in it
moth, not burned
The moth flies to the glow and is lost, but the wise one admires the glow and passes by, unburned.
My cousin is always drawn to shiny new things like a moth, but my aunt walks calmly past them all, enjoying the sight, never reaching.
A moth is drawn to the dazzle and burns, while the wise person admires the world's glitter and walks by without touching it; please write a doha on this freedom within life.
temple, swan, unattached

A swan glides past the temple pond without stopping to claim the reflection of the spire, and the wise one passes through the world's holy and unholy places alike with the same free and unclinging heart.
The swan glides past the temple and takes nothing of it, and the heart that is free does the same.
The old caretaker at our temple sweeps its floors with great care, feeds the swans at the pond, and leaves at dusk without any sense of ownership; I'd like a doha for him.
doha with a temple and a swan, about serving without being attached
net, unattached
The net is cast, the catch comes and goes, and the fisherman who watches without longing is the one at peace.
My father fishes with a net on weekends and says he is happy whether it comes back full or empty, and I wish I had his calm.
doha with a net, about taking what comes and not clinging
Write a doha where a fisherman casts his net into the flow of life and receives what comes with open hands, whether full or empty, and goes home with the same calm mind either way.
Please write a doha for a mother who looks after her family and does her best for them every day, and who nevertheless knows deep inside that she is the guest of this life, not the owner.
guest, not owner
As we cleaned out my late aunt's home, we remembered how she had given everything to the family yet seemed to hold none of it, and left as lightly as she had arrived.
Dwell in the world as a guest in a friend's home, grateful on arrival, light at the leaving.
doha about living in the world as a visitor
